correctness.rationale: For equal-length binary words, the complete order-two binomial signature is exactly (S=sum bits,J=sum positional weights), since #01=J-binomial(S,2), while #00,#11,#10 follow from ones count and total length. The Thue–Morse relation t_{2a}=t_a,t_{2a+1}=1-t_a forces each aligned two-letter pair to contain one 1. Three adjacent odd-root blocks cannot have equal ones counts, since one of their adjacent pairs starts on an even boundary and has counts h+b versus h+1-b. For m=2h with h odd, even starts reduce equality of J(mu(x))=h²-S(x) to the forbidden odd-root abelian cube; odd starts use four boundary bits, whose equal differences must all vanish, and a left-rotation moment identity gives the same forbidden cube. For m=4k, mu²(0)=0110 and mu²(1)=1001 both have two ones and moment 3, and order-2 binomial equivalence is a concatenation congruence, so any aligned concatenation length4k works for every exponent. Independent 8192-bit arithmetic-prefix calculation checked all starting positions for m<=64 and uniform aligned examples; finite tests corroborate but not replace proof for all m and exponent.
residual_risks: The theorem applies to one-sided Thue–Morse and exponent ell>=3, and does not settle all starting positions for permissible roots.
